subject: Launch intake: quota & product clarifications for NovaLabs pilot
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan@novalabs.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Launch intake: quota & product clarifications for NovaLabs pilot

Team / Evan —

Quick context: NovaLabs (DL-4721) is planning a closed beta on 2028-06-01. They expect an initial ramp to ~1.2M tokens/day over a 72-hour window on day 1 of the pilot, with sustained 200k tokens/day afterward. They want predictable latency (~250–350ms p95 on gen) and a temporary higher ingress allowance during the 72-hour ramp.

 asks:
- Temporary quota bump for the pilot window (ingress rate to handle bursts ~1200 rps peak, baseline ~200 rps).
- Confirmation whether we can enable prefix-KV pre-warming or a warmup token pool for their session cache.
- Product question: can the routing policy pin to a more performant variant (gpu-opt-4q) for the pilot and auto-fallback to a quantized variant on capacity pressure?
- Telemetry/observability: need per-route token-level cost breakdown and trace hooks available to NovaLabs for troubleshooting.

I attached a preliminary traffic-profile.json and a mutual_action_plan.xlsx that Evan shared. Evan / Maya — can you confirm the numbers are representative and whether they expect multi-region failover?

Next steps suggested: Karthik — can you coordinate a short preflight with Infra/Product tomorrow to validate the feasibility and list specific guardrails? Marissa — please capture the ask in Deal record (HubSpot) and push the Docusign SLA if required.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: traffic-profile.json (application/json)] [Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan@novalabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:16:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Launch intake: quota & product clarifications for NovaLabs pilot

Thanks Priyom — copying Infra/Product leads implicitly via Grace for product/infra validation.

A few clarifying Qs before we pull in runbook:
1) Traffic shape: is the 1.2M tokens/day concentrated into a continuous 72-hour stream or is it expected as short sharp spikes (minutes-long) within that window?
2) Are there multi-tenant concerns (many distinct end-users) that would make consistent KV-cache hit rates low? If so, the value of pre-warm is limited.
3) Do they require streaming token-by-token latency guarantees for the entire window, or is tail latency allowance acceptable on occasional fallback?

Grace — can Product/Infra confirm whether we can:
- provision a temporary dedicated capacity pool (reserved) for the 72-hour window vs a quota ramp on shared capacity; and
- expose a warmup endpoint or accept a pre-populated KV snapshot for sessions?

Evan — quick ping: if you can sketch the burst profile (attachment) as 1-minute and 1-hour percentiles that will help us size burst pools accurately.

Karthik
Sr. AM, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan@novalabs.ai>, Maya Chen <maya@novalabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Launch intake: quota & product clarifications for NovaLabs pilot

Thanks — reviewed the traffic-profile.json attachment. High-level product/infra take:

Feasibility notes:
- Temporary reserved pool: we can provision a small dedicated pool for a 72-hour window, but it requires a 72-hour lead time for GPU scheduling and an Ops change. If NovaLabs needs quicker turn-up, we can instead create a temporary higher ingress quota on shared capacity with automatic throttles and a priority routing policy.
- Warmup / KV pre-pop: we do not currently support ingesting a pre-populated KV snapshot into the runtime. However, we can provide a warmup token endpoint + an accelerated prefill policy that will prioritize prefix caching for sessions flagged in the API request headers. That will achieve similar effective cache hit improvement without snapshot import.
- Model pinning: we can route to gpu-opt-4q for the pilot but recommend a canary sequence: pin 70% traffic to gpu-opt-4q and keep 30% on q4-fallback to monitor quality and latency regressions. Automatic fallback to quantized variant is supported with routing policies.
- Observability: we can grant NovaLabs a read-only dashboard with per-route token breakdown and a tracing hook; log retention for beta customers is the standard 30d unless we enable a compliance add-on.

Operational guardrails we need from Sales/Evan:
- A minute-level burst percentile table (p50/p90/p99 for 1m and 1h) — helps size token buckets.
- Confirmed list of client IP ranges for temporary whitelisting (if they plan failover from other regions).
- Agreed SLA deviation policy (what to do if p95 > 800ms during the ramp).

Tentative next steps / timeline:
- By Mon 2028-05-14: Karthik/Priyom to provide burst percentiles and IP ranges.
- By Tue 2028-05-16: Infra to provision quota ramp plan vs reserved pool (PRD + Ops ticket).
- 48 hours before pilot: enable warmup policy + test warmup endpoint with test tokens.

I'll raise an infra ticket this afternoon and add the ops runbook. If we can get the percentile table this weekend we can favor a reserved pool.

Grace
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: ops-checklist-template.md (text) — not included]

From: Evan Brooks <evan@novalabs.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Maya Chen <maya@novalabs.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Launch intake: quota & product clarifications for NovaLabs pilot

Thanks all — attached a revised traffic profile with 1m/1h percentiles and a short note on multi-region failover. We plan primary traffic from us-east-1 and an automated failover to eu-west-1 (low volume) if latency breaches 750ms for >5 minutes.

Highlights:
- Peak minute p99: 1,150 rps (estimated) — roughly matches Priyom's peak assumption.
- Hourly p99: 320 rps.
- Concurrent distinct end-users expected to be high (many small requests), so KV hit-rate will start low and improve over 24–36 hours as sessions stabilize.

We consent to the canary pin approach and prefer the reserved pool if scheduling permits; if not, the temporary higher ingress quota on shared capacity is acceptable as long as we get an ops contact and an automated escalation path.

Action items we expect from Redwood:
1) Finalized ramp plan (reserved pool vs quota ramp) and estimated provisioning ETA.
2) Access to warmup endpoint and a short usage doc.
3) Read-only dashboard link and trace hook onboarding instructions.

Thanks — attaching traffic-profile.json and updated mutual_action_plan.xlsx.

Evan
Head of Platform, NovaLabs
